findings.detail: 'sin contar el tiempo de consumo local' renders 'excluding local consumer time'. A consumer is an actor — the local client that spends time outside the measured stream — and the translation turns it into an abstract 'consumption'. 'consumo de tokens' is house vocabulary elsewhere in this catalogue, so the word itself is fine; what is lost is whose time is excluded, in a help string whose whole job is to define exactly what the rate does and does not include.
findings.remediation: …por debajo de esta tasa de tokens de salida por segundo, sin contar el tiempo que tarda el consumidor local.

findings.detail: 'puede iniciar una caché de prompts en frío' calques 'may start a cold prompt cache': a cache does not get started cold, it starts cold. The catalogue already has the parallel 'costarte una caché de prompts en caliente', so this is preference, not term drift.
findings.remediation: Cambiar de host puede hacer que la caché de prompts arranque en frío.

noted_outside_scope.topic: catalogue-wide rendering of 'phone access' as 'acceso telefónico'
noted_outside_scope.detail: 'acceso telefónico' is the established rendering (wire.slash.mobile: 'Acceso telefónico de Radient'), so it is consistent and not a finding against this namespace. A Spanish reader can also parse it as telephone/dial-up access; if the wave wants 'acceso desde el teléfono' it must change every surface at once, never this namespace alone.

noted_outside_scope.topic: es guide kept-English list names 'cache'; the shipped catalogue consistently writes 'caché'
noted_outside_scope.detail: wire.settings.json uses 'caché' in ~40 prose strings ('caché de prompts', 'TTL de caché'). This namespace's 'caché' follows the catalogue, so it is not drift introduced here; the conflict is between i18n/style-guides/es.md and the shipped copy and needs a wave-level decision (amend the list or fix the catalogue), not a one-namespace patch.
